title: Loops
summary: Learn how to repeat actions in code.

steps.title: Why Loops?
steps.markdownContent: Loops let you repeat actions without copying code. If you want an LED to blink 10 times, you don't need 10 blink commands.

steps.title: For Loops
steps.markdownContent: A `for` loop counts. Example: `for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { ... }` runs 5 times, with `i` acting as a counter.

steps.title: While Loops
steps.markdownContent: A `while` loop runs as long as a condition is true. It can be infinite if the condition never becomes false. Arduino's main `loop()` is an intentional infinite loop!

steps.title: Visualize a Loop
steps.markdownContent: Visualize a `for` loop counting from 0 to 4.

steps.title: Predict Loop Behavior
steps.markdownContent: How many times will this loop run?

steps.markdownContent: Test what you learned about loops.

questions.question: Why do we use loops?
options: To repeat actions without writing duplicate code
questions.explanation: Loops automate repetition, keeping code clean and short.

questions.question: What is `i` in a typical `for` loop?
questions.explanation: The counter variable tracks how many times the loop has run.

questions.question: What kind of loop does Arduino use continuously?
questions.explanation: The main loop() function repeats forever to keep processing.
